narrative: Material PL3__MEE0F34F exhibits a bimodal daily demand pattern: most working days see approximately 2,300 units consumed, while a minority of days show near-zero demand, yielding a mean of ~1,717 units/day and CV of 0.60. Lead times are highly variable (CV=0.639, range 1.09–5.62 days), dominating the combined uncertainty. The (r,Q) continuous-review policy is recommended: trigger replenishment at 10,623 units on hand, ordering 15,042 units each time (capacity-constrained from EOQ of 44,532). This policy maintains 95% service level while cutting total annual inventory costs by 84.3% versus the current SAP baseline.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: EOQ of 44,532 exceeds available space; order quantity capped at 15,042 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Material has consistently high daily volumes (~2,300 units on active days) with near-continuous demand, making a continuous-review (r,Q) model appropriate. The policy triggers an order when inventory falls to the reorder point r=10,623, placing a fixed quantity Q=15,042. This avoids the over-ordering of periodic-review models while respecting MOQ and capacity constraints.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is the binding constraint: the warehouse limit of 19,631.7 units caps the order quantity at 15,042 (safety_stock + OQ = 19,631 ≤ 19,631.7). If demand volatility spikes or a large delivery arrives during high-stock periods, the warehouse may be temporarily exceeded. Recommend reviewing max_storage_units quarterly.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (1,995) + safety_stock (4,589) = 6,584 < max_storage_units (19,631.7); no MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
